Changelog

gsm.ctas (development version)

Source data always reaches ctasapp (#39)

ctasapp now gets source data for every field: when CTAS scores it, when CTAS drops the timeseries, when the field only has a missingness score, and when a field’s values are all NA. Each metric workflow ships its Standardize_Domain() output as the untransformed frame, so source rows don’t depend on whether the CTAS run succeeds. The ctasapp upload contract is unchanged; only columns were added.

Root causes

  • Transform_Range() dropped rows. It removed rows with an NA value or an unusable reference range. ANISO has numeric values but no reference ranges, so it disappeared completely. COLOR is text-only and was dropped the same way.
  • Only some metrics shipped source rows. range_normalized shipped its transformed rows as untransformed, so NA rows were already gone. numeric and ratio_missing shipped nothing.
  • BindResults_CTAS() dropped rows without a value. It removed every untransformed row where both original_value and original_category were NA, and it didn’t de-duplicate across metrics.
  • A CTAS failure cost the whole metric. An error inside CTAS, including CTAS dropping every timeseries, aborted the metric workflow and lost its input and untransformed.
  • ctasapp ignores missingness rows for source data. Its Source Data table only attaches untransformed to input rows that aren’t missingness rows. A field with only a MISS_ timeseries, such as COLOR, therefore showed no source data.

Changes

  • Standardize_Domain()
    • Always adds original_value, lower, upper and original_category.
    • New argument strCharCol (e.g. LBSTRESC) fills original_category where the numeric result is NA, so text results like COLOR “N” or ECGINT “ABNORMAL” stay visible.
    • Drops no rows, except for subjects missing from dfSubjects.
  • Transform_Range()
    • No longer drops rows. Rows with an NA value or an unusable range keep result = NA, so CTAS’s missingness threshold applies.
    • New argument dMaxShareMissingRange (default 0.5). When more than that share of a field’s values has no usable range, the field is emitted as raw NUM_<field> with parameter_category_3 = "numeric". ANISO is handled this way.
    • Fields with no values at all are kept with NA results and listed in a message.
  • Transform_Missing(): lists fields that are 100% missing for all subjects in a cli message. The MISS_ output is unchanged.
  • BindResults_CTAS(..., "untransformed")
    • Removes value, result, low, high, parameter_id and parameter_category_3 before binding.
    • Keeps rows with no reported value.
    • De-duplicates on (study, subject_id, parameter_category_2, timepoint_1_name), keeping the copy with the most filled-in original_* columns.
  • Analyze_CTAS(): new bStopOnError argument. When FALSE, an error from CTAS becomes a warning and an empty results frame (EmptyCTASResults()), so input and untransformed are still shipped. Input validation still aborts.
  • Workflows
    • All four metric YAMLs ship untransformed and set StopOnError: false.
    • range_normalized.yaml adds MaxShareMissingRange: 0.5.
    • categorical.yaml no longer needs its SQL de-duplication step.
    • The LB, VS and EG mappings and metric specs now carry *STRESC.
  • Docs: roxygen, man/, Cookbook and .github/copilot-instructions.md.

Effect on the sample data

  • ANISO: scored as NUM_ANISO.
  • COLOR: has RANGE_COLOR input rows with NA results plus MISS_COLOR. Its 830 untransformed rows show original_category = "N".
  • ECGINT: has numeric input rows with NA results, and its source rows show NORMAL/ABNORMAL.
  • Coverage: every input field appears in untransformed, and the join keys are unique.

Known limitation

MISS_ ratios still look only at *STRESN, so text-only fields such as COLOR and ECGINT show 100% missing. Counting a *STRESC result as reported is left for a follow-up.

Tests tagged #39

Standardize_Domain results must match source data, keeping every row and field (#29, #39) (test-validation.R)

  • Data: bundled dm, vs and lb.
  • Preparation: Standardize_Domain() on VS, and on LB with strLowCol, strHighCol and strCharCol = "LBSTRESC".
  • Comparison: the output’s original_value, lower, upper and original_category are mapped back to LBSTRESN, LBSTNRLO, LBSTNRHI and LBSTRESC. The source side keeps LBSTRESC only where LBSTRESN is NA.
  • Alignment: both frames are sorted on all columns.
  • Expected: the mapped-back frame equals the source exactly, so no rows or fields are lost.

Transform_Range results must match source data without dropping any field (#32, #39) (test-validation.R)

  • Data: bundled dm and lb.
  • Preparation: Standardize_Domain() with ranges, then Transform_Range() with the default threshold.
  • Comparison: NUM_ fields are mapped back to the raw value and RANGE_ fields are de-normalised. The expected frame is derived from the source: it applies the fallback rule per field and sets unusable-range values to NA.
  • Alignment: both frames are sorted on all columns.
  • Expected: the frames are equal, every LBTESTCD is present (COLOR included), and ANISO is NUM_ANISO.

Write_ctasapp files meet ctasapp file requirements and carry source rows for every field (#33, #39) (test-validation.R)

  • Data: the full bundled data (dm, lb, vs, eg, rs, queries, pd).
  • Preparation: the mapping, metric and reporting workflows, then Write_ctasapp() to parquet.
  • Comparison 1: the untransformed keys are compared with the distinct keys from the mapped LB, VS, EG, RS and BMI data, restricted to known subjects.
  • Comparison 2: the test rebuilds ctasapp’s prepare_ts_data_multi() join: input without ratio_missing rows, left-joined to de-duplicated untransformed on the join keys.
  • Expected:
    • the untransformed keys are unique and equal the source keys;
    • every parameter_category_2 in input appears in the joined Source Data table. This check failed on COLOR before the Transform_Range() change.

an all-NA field keeps MISS_ input and raw untransformed rows (#39) (test_workflow.R)

  • Data: a 6-site slice of the pharmaversesdtm data, stacked into two studies, with EG including ECGINT (a text-only field).
  • Preparation: the mapping and metric workflows.
  • Comparison: the MISS_ECGINT input and the bound untransformed rows for ECGINT, against the distinct study/subject/visit combinations in the source.
  • Expected:
    • MISS_ECGINT is 1 everywhere;
    • untransformed has one ECGINT row per source key, with NA original_value and non-NA original_category.

a field CTAS drops still ships input and untransformed (#39) (test_workflow.R)

  • Data: the same workflow test data as above.
  • Preparation: the numeric metric workflow, which receives ECGINT with NA results only.
  • Comparison: results against input and untransformed for ECGINT.
  • Expected: ECGINT is missing from results but present in both input and untransformed.

Transform_Missing keeps an all-NA field and names it in a message (#39) (test-Transform.R)

  • Data: a small synthetic frame with COLOR (all NA) and ALT (partly NA).
  • Preparation: Transform_Missing().
  • Comparison: the emitted message and the MISS_ output.
  • Expected: the message names COLOR, COLOR’s ratio is 1 at every visit, and both MISS_COLOR and MISS_ALT are present.
